result:
No leftover temp files. The implementation is complete. Summary of the changes made across the codebase:

**Service layer** (`src/server/services/member-service.ts`): added `suspendMember`, `reinstateMember`, and `MemberSuspendedError`, plus updated `assertLastOwnerRetained` so the last-owner invariant ignores suspended owners.

**Repository layer**: added `setMemberStatus` and widened `countActiveMembers` to count suspended alongside active members (`member-repository.ts`); widened the seat query in `recomputeUsage` the same way (`usage-repository.ts`); excluded suspended members' orgs from `listOrgsForUser` (`organization-repository.ts`).

**Events/audit**: added `member.suspended`/`member.reinstated` to `TaskflowEventMap`, `ActivityAction`, the activity zod schema, activity labels, and wired both into `registerActivityListeners`.

**Side effects of suspension**: `notify()` now skips suspended recipients (the single chokepoint for all notification creation); `listDigestRecipients` skips them for the daily digest; comment mention resolution drops suspended members from both `@handle` resolution and client-supplied ids; `createIssue`/`assignIssue` throw `MemberSuspendedError` when the assignee is suspended.

Existing checks (`resolveActor`, `resolveActorForOrg`, `switchActiveOrg`) already treated any non-`"active"` status as unable to act, so they needed no changes — reinstatement (flipping status back to `"active"`) transparently restores all of this.

Verified with a temporary end-to-end test (now removed) covering suspend/reinstate idempotency, self/outrank refusals, the extended last-owner invariant, seat counting, org-switcher exclusion, assignment/mention/notification blocking, and audit logging — then confirmed `tsc --noEmit` is clean and all 617 existing tests still pass.
